chapter: The Tristano group and leaving for Kenton
title: Warne Marsh, the Tristano circle and making a living
summary: Talk of Warne Marsh recordings and a book, the 'cult' view of Konitz, and his desire to work in the world rather than just practice.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Yeah. They started out with this tune at this tempo [taps a fast tempo] and [on] some other tunes I’ve heard Warne with Niels Henning and Al Levitt playing very fast tempos very flawlessly. Do you know the book this man in Australia wrote?
Safford Chamberlain, the biography of Warne?

No, the man in Australia wrote a book called “Out of Nowhere” and assumed the voice of Warne Marsh, scarily so. He obviously knew Warne. He would have to [in order] to say the things he said . . . so close to home. But somehow or other, he had summed up that I had reached, as Warne Marsh, what I had set out to do. It’s like he was saying that he’s finished his work and now he could leave town.
Supposedly that was the last tune he played and then he had that heart attack right?
Yeah. The way it was voiced in the obituary sounded a little bit like a put on of the “Tristano cult” playing their half a dozen tunes.
You were the one, more so that the other people of the ‘cult’, who went furthest from the nest and apparently that wasn’t appreciated.

The idea was to stay at home and practice and play with fellow students, and get a day job. I wasn’t about to do that. I mean here I am playing with people all other the place who are enjoying sharing my experience and I enjoyed their enthusiasm, I’m getting paid so I can pay the rent and all that, so why are they putting me down? I’m pretty lucky.
You’re making a living as a player. What a concept.
That was the name of the game, ultimately. Enough people support you that you could keep moving around . . . be able to do it more than ever. Now they just want to know if I can get through a set.
And their very pleased that I can and I am too.
